questions.stem: Which group marks a compound as a carboxylic acid?

options.text: -COOH at the end of a chain
options.explanation: The carboxyl arrangement of atoms is the defining feature of the whole family.
An -OH alone marks an alcohol, one step short of the acid group.
That arrangement is the ester link, not the acid group.
A C=C bond marks an alkene and has nothing to do with acidity.

questions.stem: In the general formula CnH2n+1COOH, what does n count?

options.text: Only the carbons in the alkyl chain
options.explanation: The acid carbon sits outside the count, which is exactly why methanoic acid has n = 0.

options.text: Every carbon in the molecule including the acid carbon
options.explanation: Counting the acid carbon would shift every formula by one carbon.
Hydrogens follow as 2n+1; n itself counts carbons in the chain.
The acid always carries two oxygens regardless of n.

questions.stem: What is the value of n for methanoic acid, HCOOH?

options.text: Zero, because there is no alkyl chain at all
options.explanation: The single carbon present belongs to the acid group, so the chain count is empty.

options.text: One, because one carbon is visible in the formula
options.explanation: That one carbon is the acid carbon, which never enters the count.

options.text: Two, counting the carbon and one oxygen
options.explanation: n never counts oxygen atoms under any reading.

options.text: It is undefined for the first member
options.explanation: The formula applies cleanly; n is simply zero for the shortest member.

questions.stem: What does the R stand for in the shortened formula RCOOH?

options.text: A hydrocarbon chain of any length
options.explanation: R is the placeholder for the varying chain that the acid group sits upon.
Metals appear in salts of these acids, never inside RCOOH itself.
The group is written separately as COOH; R is everything else.
Water is a product of some reactions here but is never the R group.

questions.stem: Which writing of the family formula is the shortened form?

options.explanation: Replacing the chain detail with R compresses CnH2n+1COOH to its shortest honest form.
That recipe belongs to the alkane family, not to the acids.
That is the alcohol shorthand; the acids need the full -COOH.
That recipe fits alkenes, not the acid family.

questions.stem: Write down the family formula that every carboxylic acid member follows.
questions.modelAnswer: The general formula is CnH2n+1COOH, which can be shortened to RCOOH.

questions.stem: How many alkyl carbons does the family formula count for methanoic acid, HCOOH?
questions.modelAnswer: For methanoic acid the alkyl chain count n is zero — HCOOH carries just the carboxyl carbon.

questions.stem: Explain why the n in CnH2n+1COOH does not count the carboxyl carbon itself.
questions.modelAnswer: Because n counts only the alkyl chain; the COOH group is written separately at the end, so n never includes the carboxyl carbon.

questions.stem: Propanoic acid has three carbons in total. Using the family formula CnH2n+1COOH, state the value of n for propanoic acid.
questions.misconceptionClass: applying n to a named member
questions.modelAnswer: n equals two for propanoic acid — two alkyl carbons plus the carboxyl carbon gives three in total.

options.explanation: Three carbons in total give the prop- stem with the oic acid ending.
Ethanoic acid carries only two carbons, CH3COOH.
Butanoic acid carries four carbons, one more than shown.
The -ol ending marks an alcohol; this structure ends in the acid group.

questions.stem: Which structure belongs to butanoic acid?

options.explanation: Four carbons in total means three in the chain plus the acid carbon.
That two-carbon structure is ethanoic acid.
That single-carbon structure is methanoic acid.
That three-carbon structure is propanoic acid.

questions.stem: How many carbon atoms does ethanoic acid contain in total?

options.text: Two, one in the chain and one in the acid group
options.explanation: The CH3 contributes one carbon and the -COOH contributes the other.

options.text: One, because only the CH3 is visible
options.explanation: The acid carbon is easy to miss but is present in the -COOH.
Three carbons in total would make it propanoic acid.
Four carbons in total belong to butanoic acid.

options.text: An aqueous solution of ethanoic acid at about 5 percent
options.explanation: The household liquid is a dilute watery solution of the acid, not the pure substance.
Pure ethanoic acid is a concentrated liquid, far stronger than any kitchen bottle.
Ethanol is the starting material of the acid, but vinegar contains the acid itself.
Citric acid souring fruit is a different acid; vinegar is firmly ethanoic.

questions.stem: A student draws displayed formulae of the first four acids. Which rule keeps every member unbranched?

options.text: One straight chain with the -COOH group at the end
options.explanation: Unbranched members run a single chain with the acid group terminal.

options.text: The -COOH group sits in the middle of the chain
options.explanation: A mid-chain group would break the acid pattern these members follow.

options.text: Side branches appear from three carbons upward
options.explanation: The first four members carry no branches at all.

options.text: Rings form once four carbons are present
options.explanation: These acids stay open chains; rings belong to other families.

questions.stem: Name the first four carboxylic acids in order of chain length.
questions.modelAnswer: Methanoic acid, ethanoic acid, propanoic acid and butanoic acid.

questions.stem: What is vinegar, in terms of its composition?
questions.modelAnswer: Vinegar is an aqueous solution of ethanoic acid, at about 5 percent by volume.

questions.stem: Explain how the name ethanoic acid encodes the chain length of the acid.
questions.misconceptionClass: naming law alkan plus oic acid
questions.modelAnswer: The name is built as alkan plus oic acid, and the ethan root stands for the two-carbon alkyl chain.

questions.stem: Give the molecular formula of the acid that follows ethanoic acid in the series, and name it.
questions.modelAnswer: The next member is propanoic acid, CH3CH2COOH, with three carbons in total.
